gui.grindless.guide.title: Field Guide
gui.grindless.guide.bootstrap.title: Bootstrap
gui.grindless.guide.bootstrap.body: Your Quest Book arrives automatically when you join while your starter kit is unclaimed. If your inventory is full, make one empty slot for delivery. Hold and use the book, select Free starter supplies and press Claim free kit. No crafting or commands are needed: each player can explicitly claim one finite kit of stone, wood, food and basic workshop supplies. Make room for the whole kit; a full inventory rejects the claim without consuming it or dropping items. After claiming, craft a replacement Quest Book if you lose it. Check the current recipes below and keep the materials needed for each build. Construct the Crank Handle, Hand Pump and ceramic workshop, then establish geological collection, bioculture and biomass power. The Crank Handle supplies limited local startup work to eligible F0 process machines; it is not fuel and cannot power the Research Terminal. The Multitool rotates or relocates machines; it never mines. Make glass, copper and redstone through the workshop instead of treating them as required starting supplies. The Hand Crank Dynamo and finite-vein Crude Extractor offer an optional exploration or emergency branch. Ore veins run out, so do not rely on that branch for continuing supply. Make an Atlas when you have its ingredients.
gui.grindless.guide.workshop.title: Ceramic Workshop
gui.grindless.guide.settling.title: Open Settling Line
gui.grindless.guide.settling.body: Place a Settling Channel behind the Settling Trough controller and a Settling Screen behind the channel. Face the line the same way and keep air above its parts; the controller can take a hopper above. Only the controller has item, water and power interfaces. Its current dirt, wet-aggregate and flint-separation recipes are listed below with their quantities. Clay feeds the Mixer and gravel feeds the Quern. Recover eligible output water through a Clay Conduit for reuse; recovery does not create a new source. Flint has no established use in this T0 route. You may keep it as optional stock or discard it normally. Wrong-facing, missing or covered parts pause work without losing the batch. The Multitool rotates parts and the controller reports the exact fault.
gui.grindless.guide.workshop.body: The Quern mills gravel to sand and recovers ceramic grog. A Hand Pump needs a water source in front or below and exports in its facing direction. Feed the Clay Mixer with clay, water and the sand or grog named by its current recipe. Build a 2x2x2 brick chamber with the Firing Chamber controller at the front-left bottom cell and bricks in the other cells. Follow the recipes below for heat, atmosphere, fuel and yields. Reuse grog in the grog-body recipe with fresh clay and water. Insulators support cores, tanks, Clay Conduits, belts and manipulators. Feed the chamber from its free front/left faces and extract below; repairing the structure preserves work. Slag from metal reduction has no established T0 use, and its future usefulness is uncertain. You may discard it normally or keep it if you wish; storage is optional, and no automatic disposal is provided.
gui.grindless.guide.relay.title: Relay Matrix
gui.grindless.guide.relay.body: Make a ceramic Data Core and calibrate it in a powered Research Terminal. The Crank Handle cannot charge that terminal. Finish T0 with the manual five-Relay-Matrix craft using the Calibrated Data Core; the Assembly Bench does not fabricate a Matrix. These Relay Matrices are physical items, not an unlocked permission. The recipes below show current ingredients, yields, time and power. Before relying on the later powered factory, arrange its fuel, water and item handling: owning a Matrix does not power or supply those machines.
gui.grindless.guide.power.title: Voltaic Power
gui.grindless.guide.power.body: Burn charcoal or coal in the Thermal Generator for unattended F1 power. A Flux Pylon MK I covers the first room; it is infrastructure, so it does not consume a Matrix. The Hand Crank stays useful for isolated F0 work, but the factory begins when power reaches the Pulverizer, Arc Furnace, Press and Assembler through the pylon.
gui.grindless.guide.extraction.title: Surveyed Extraction
gui.grindless.guide.extraction.body: Use the Prospector's Scanner before placing a Terrestrial Extractor. A surveyed ChunkVein is finite, but extraction is automated and no longer asks you to hand-mine each unit. Build another outpost when a field runs down; the Factory World has the same surveyed fields beneath its clean grass floor.
gui.grindless.guide.factory.title: First Factory
gui.grindless.guide.factory.body: The Pulverizer turns cobblestone into sand in six seconds. The Arc Furnace vitrifies sand into glass and reduces mineral feed with carbon. The Press makes plates, rods, gears and copper coils with reusable dies. Those parts make the Assembler. Once it exists, feed glass, copper, redstone and a Calibrated Data Core to repeat the five-Matrix batch in twenty seconds.
gui.grindless.guide.renewables.title: Renewable Inputs
gui.grindless.guide.renewables.body: Build continuing supply around Grindless machines: a water-fed Geological Collector supplies aggregate and clay; the Biocultivator uses aggregate, water and daylight to grow biomass; the Biomass Dynamo fuels F0 work from that biomass. Collection needs a geological rock bed in the Overworld or Factory. Culture needs the same dimensions, open sky and enough daylight. Do not assume the line will keep running at night or resume on its own after restarting. The Hand Pump needs a water source in front or below. Mill aggregate for stone and gravel, settle it for mineral feed and redstone, and use biomass for boards, sticks, paper and firing carbon. The formed ceramic workshop makes glass and metals through the recipes below. Reuse grog and recovered water where the recipes allow; replace losses through the pump and source machines. Gathering finite supplies and using vanilla alternatives can help with startup or an emergency. Use this machine loop for continuing supply instead of depending on vanilla cobblestone generators or tree farms. A recipe list does not show whether your own machines have power, water and a suitable site: check their status before relying on the line.
gui.grindless.guide.logistics.title: Logistics and Heat
gui.grindless.guide.logistics.body: Conveyor Belts move items through the first factory; splitters, mergers, sorters and tunnel belts organise the line without power. A Basic Tank and Clay Conduit hold and move ambient water. The Kiln handles low-temperature fired feeds. Use the Process Atlas for exact live recipes and conditions: it describes a route, but leaves the layout decision to you.
gui.grindless.guide.factory_world.title: Factory World
gui.grindless.guide.factory_world.body: After the Assembler can replace consumed matrices, craft a Factory Portal with glass, copper, redstone and one Relay Matrix. It leads to a flat grass construction world at permanent midday, with no weather or hostile spawns. Return through its arrival portal to the exact portal that sent you. Its resource fields remain finite and surveyed, so clean terrain is never free material.
gui.grindless.guide.industrial.title: Industrial Matrix
gui.grindless.guide.industrial.body: T1 ends with a physical F2 Relay Matrix, not a permission. In the Assembler, combine one F1 Relay Matrix, a Machine Casing, four renewable glass and a Flux Cell. The former Matrix is consumed: its relay control is carried forward, the casing is the structure, glass is the dielectric and the cell is the power coupling. This is the hand-off to Industrial; do not expect an F2 machine to be hand-crafted.

gui.grindless.shop.detail.stone: The Quern's dry aggregate route yields more stone plus gravel. Use this only for recovery.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_ston: Lost your first supplies? Dig ordinary dirt by hand. This costly restart needs only the already-claimed starter quest, not a working machine.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_wood: Paid restart wood from manually dug dirt. Establish fibreboard production instead of repeatedly digging terrain.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_wate: Lost both starter buckets? Manually dug dirt buys one replacement filled bucket, before any pump or industrial stock. No claim is reset or paid twice.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.gravel: Direct dry aggregate processing also gives cobblestone. This convenience exchange gives no coproducts.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.sand: The Quern makes sand from gravel. Paid convenience does not replace that route.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.clay: Geological collection already supplies clay alongside aggregate. No insulators or finished cores are sold.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.wood: Fibreboard already works as boards in Grindless recipes. Vanilla wood is optional and costs more equivalent boards.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.food: A small food recovery batch paid with real biomass. The original one-time starter food remains unchanged.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.sapling: Optional tree growing and landscaping. The factory's canonical wood substitute is mod-owned fibreboard.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.seeds: Optional farming. No mandatory T0 route depends on growing vanilla crops.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.water: One real empty bucket is consumed and returned filled. No new bucket is created. The Hand Pump remains the normal supply.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.fuel: One emergency charcoal. The Firing Chamber's native biomass-to-charcoal batch is much more efficient.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bricks: Unlocked after ceramics. Grog remains reusable in ceramic bodies; trading bricks back into grog loses the other payment.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.dirt: For building. Wet aggregate processing gives more dirt per aggregate and also supplies metals and redstone.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.grass: Optional terrain blocks. This does not turn vanilla farming into a mandatory production source.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.glass: Only after physical calibration. You must already have made the first glass and calibrated core yourself.

gui.grindless.quest.lesson.starter_suppl:
Arrival: your Quest Book is restored on join or respawn. Leave one main-inventory slot if delivery is waiting. Hold it, select Free starter supplies and press Claim free kit. No paper, commands, village or currency is needed.

Each player can explicitly claim one finite kit. Make room for all eleven stacks; insufficient space changes nothing and drops nothing. Reserve construction supplies and water while you establish geological collection, bioculture and biomass power. Recovery never resets this claim.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.quest_book_he:
The Quest Book is your teaching and progress entry point. Select a quest, read Learn / recipes, then record its checklist or claim its listed reward. Locked T0 lessons remain readable; prerequisites concern claims, not machine permissions.

Lost the book after claiming the kit? Rejoin or respawn with one free main-inventory slot for utility-only recovery, or craft a replacement using the live recipe. Existing books, including one in your offhand, prevent duplicate delivery. The Process Atlas remains a recipe viewer, not the retired Guide.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.superflat:
Superflat is building space, not a promise of visible ore blocks. Use the finite starter bridge, then establish Grindless producers for continuing supplies. A Geological Collector accepts a bedrock or other valid geological bed; deposits used by optional extractors are virtual chunk data, not terrain ore.

Do not make a village, mob farm, vanilla cobblestone generator or tree farm the permanent critical route. Leave space for water, a rock-bed Collector, open-sky culture and a repairable workshop. Check each machine's actual site and status rather than assuming a flat world supplies everything.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.construction:
Reserve stone, boards, sticks, clay and bricks before spending the starter bridge. A crafting table and furnace support construction; the chamber needs brick blocks in addition to its crafted controller. The live recipes below show the actual batch costs.

Later, dry aggregate supplies stone and gravel, fired clay supplies bricks, and fibreboard replaces ordinary boards in Grindless recipes. Keep enough material to rebuild the source machines. A furnace in your inventory is only a construction checklist, not proof that the renewable workshop is established.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.multitool:
The Multitool is a wrench, not a pickaxe. Use it on a Grindless block to rotate it; sneak-use relocates the machine with its saved inventory and state. Have room for the returned item and recover any dropped stack.

Rotate pumps, controllers, belts and trough parts to correct their direction. Moving a controller invalidates its old assembled shape until you rebuild it. Lost tools are crafted again from stone and sticks; no quest reset or advanced component is required.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.manual_work:
The reusable Crank Handle provides %s FU of bounded local startup work per admitted use, with a %s-tick cooldown. Use it on eligible F0 process machines after supplying their inputs, water and valid structure. It is not fuel, portable stored energy or an unlimited automated source.

If a machine will not start, read its missing-input, fluid, output or site fault before cranking again. It cannot charge the Research Terminal. Establish biomass-powered F0 supply rather than turning repeated manual clicks into the permanent factory.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.crank:
Optional exploration/emergency branch: the Hand Crank Dynamo and Crude Extractor spend iron that the renewable workshop does not require. This Dynamo is separate from the handheld Crank Handle.

Operate the Dynamo's crank to supply a connected F0 consumer. Missing connection or stored work can leave the extractor idle. Keep this branch optional; geological collection, bioculture and biomass power are the continuing T0 supply route.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.extractor:
Optional finite extraction: place the Crude Extractor in a chunk with a compatible virtual deposit and provide F0 power from the Dynamo. Clear its output and inspect its deposit/status before expecting material.

A deposit can run out, and moving to another field is not a renewable source. Do not spend the only construction stock chasing a missing vein. Return to geological aggregate, wet separation and biomass-supported workshop processing for continuing materials.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.quern:
The Quern performs dry milling and ceramic recovery. Gravel becomes sand; mineral aggregate becomes construction stone and gravel. Grog and unfired recovery have separate recipes, so use the exact input batch shown below.

Supply F0 power or bounded Crank Handle work, and leave room for every output. Idle usually means the input does not match; starved work needs power, while a full output needs clearing. Sand feeds wet ceramic bodies and glass; aggregate products rebuild the workshop.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.water:
The Hand Pump runs without FU or manual cranking. It needs a WATER-tagged source in front or directly below and exports through its facing side. Placing the source below leaves its output side free for a machine or conduit.

If water does not arrive, check for an actual source block, rotate the pump, inspect the receiving side and clear incompatible stored fluid. Use storage and Clay Conduits as needed. Supply losses from the pump; recovered output water alone does not create a source.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.clay_mixer:
The Clay Mixer combines clay, water and the sand or grog named by the selected recipe into unfired ceramic bodies. Its other wet recipe turns biomass into fibreboard. The live rows give quantities, agitation and F0 work.

Connect water, load a complete input batch and supply power or startup Handle work. No fluid, a missing second ingredient or blocked output prevents progress. Send unfired bodies to a formed Firing Chamber; keep fresh clay available even when recycling grog.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.grog:
Grog is useful ceramic aggregate, not a replacement for fresh clay or water. The Quern recovers it from brick items or fired insulators; firing insulators also returns a grog by-product. Use the grog-body Mixer recipe for the next ceramic batch.

A separate Quern recipe recovers clay and sand from a full batch of unfired bodies. Do not grind your last needed insulator before constructing tanks, transport and cores. The recipe rows distinguish recovery inputs, outputs and fresh make-up requirements.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.firing:
The plain Firing Chamber is a 2x2x2 volume: its controller is the front-left bottom cell and the other cells are brick blocks. Bottom, front to back: C B / B B. Top: B B / B B. Rotate the complete plan with the controller; exact local offsets follow below.

Feed the named material and carbon fuel, provide F0 work and room for all outputs. The chamber regulates each supported recipe's heat and atmosphere; do not substitute a missing fuel or invalid structure with more cranking. Missing or unloaded cells pause work; repair the shape. Use its ceramics, glass, metals and charcoal in the next workshop steps.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.ceramics:
Make unfired bodies in the water-fed Mixer, then fire them with carbon in the assembled chamber. The insulator recipe produces both insulators and reusable grog; leave output space for both. Exact yields, heat, atmosphere and work are shown below.

Insulators enable Data Cores, tanks, conduits, belts and manipulators. Reserve construction stock before recycling. If firing is blocked, check the formed shape, complete fuel/input batch, water upstream, power and every output slot. This inventory objective does not certify a successful firing run.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.geological_co:
The Geological Collector turns supplied water and F0 work into mineral aggregate plus clay. Place it on a valid geological rock bed in the Overworld or Factory dimension; bedrock works in Superflat. Check the site fault before adding more work.

Use bounded Handle work for startup, then Biomass Dynamo supply for continuing collection. Feed water and clear both outputs. Clay goes to ceramics and aggregate splits between dry construction supply, wet minerals and culture; collection is renewable only while all of its inputs and site remain supplied.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.aggregate:
Mineral aggregate is the junction between construction, minerals and biomass. Mill it dry for stone and gravel, settle it wet for mineral feeds and redstone, or feed it to the Biocultivator. The live rows show the distinct yields and water/work demands.

Do not send your only aggregate to a route that starves the others. Reserve culture feed and replacement construction stock, and use the Collector for continuing supply. Inventory possession proves neither collection uptime nor a self-sustaining factory.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.settling:
Place a Settling Channel directly behind the Trough controller and a Settling Screen behind the channel. Face all three the same way and keep air above the channel and screen. The controller may accept a hopper above. Exact rotated local cells follow below.

Only the controller supplies the ordinary process interfaces. Feed a complete wet batch and F0 work; inspect missing, wrong-facing, covered or unloaded-cell faults. Repairing the line preserves paid work. Use the wet-separation lesson for its actual materials, by-products and output-water recovery.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.water_recover:
Wet recipes differ: dirt settling returns clay, gravel and recoverable water; wet aggregate supplies mineral feeds, redstone, dirt, gravel and recoverable water. Flint separation has its own water cost and no returned-water output. Read the actual live row rather than assuming every wet recipe recycles water.

Recover eligible output through the controller's output interface and Clay Conduit into compatible storage or a consumer. Do not drain unmarked input water as though it were newly produced output. Refill losses from the pump. Flint is optional stock with no established T0 consumer; keep or discard it normally.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.mineral_feed:
Wet aggregate supplies iron and copper mineral feed plus redstone. Reduce the accepted raw-material tag with carbon in the formed Firing Chamber. Its recipe sets the supported heat, reducing atmosphere, F0 work and metal/slag outputs. Do not confuse a mineral feed with a finished ingot.

Copper builds transport, storage, biomass power and the final Matrix; redstone enters cores and Matrix assembly. Slag has no established T0 consumer and uncertain future usefulness: keep or discard it normally. No automatic disposal or required hoarding is implied. Clear every output before another batch.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biocultivator:
The Biocultivator consumes aggregate, water and F0 work to produce biomass. It needs the Overworld or Factory dimension, open sky and enough daylight. A roof, darkness, night or the wrong dimension is a site fault, not missing cranking.

Place it where sky access stays clear and supply its inputs before depending on biomass. Do not assume overnight or restart autonomy: inspect the real state and retain reserve feed/fuel. Biomass supports both construction materials and continuing power.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biomass:
Allocate biomass between fibreboard, paper, charcoal and direct Biomass Dynamo fuel. The live rows show its source and processing batches. Burning all of it can starve the materials needed to extend or repair your source line.

Keep water, aggregate and daylight culture supplied. Use the Quern for paper, the Mixer for fibreboard and the formed chamber for charcoal. This mod-owned loop replaces a permanent dependency on vanilla tree or mob farms, but a stocked inventory alone does not prove that your own loop keeps running.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.fibreboard:
Mix biomass with water for fibreboard. Fibreboard is accepted by the Grindless boards tag; it does not change vanilla planks recipes. Mill fibreboard into sticks and biomass into paper. Fire the separate biomass recipe in a formed chamber for charcoal.

Supply F0 work, fresh water where named and clear all outputs. Boards and sticks rebuild primitive machines; paper recrafts a lost Quest Book, and charcoal feeds firing. Do not expect one machine or one biomass recipe to produce all four materials.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biomass_dynam:
The Biomass Dynamo burns biomass for F0 output at %s FU/t for %s ticks per item. It uses physical fuel; opening a quest does not power it. Build it with the live recipe, keep its biomass input stocked and connect the consumer through the supported energy interface.

Use this supply for Collector, culture, workshop and Research Terminal work instead of permanent manual cranking. If consumers are starved, inspect fuel, connection, available output and competing demand. Keep a startup reserve; daylight and water upstream still matter.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.fluid_logisti:
Optional buffering: a Basic Tank stores compatible ambient fluid; Clay Conduits move it between real endpoints. Use the live crafts and the machine's fill/side feedback rather than treating a tank item as proof of stored water. Keep hot or incompatible fluids out of primitive water infrastructure.

Connect the pump's facing output to an accepting side. Check contents, free capacity, direction and ownership of recovered output when flow stops. Relocate with the Multitool to preserve saved machine state; verify contents after placement. Buffering supports the source loop but does not create water or replace the pump.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.conveyors:
Optional item routing: Conveyor Belts move items in their facing direction without FU. Rotate with the Multitool and feed a real receiving inventory or another compatible belt. Primitive crafts make useful batches; the live recipe owns the count.

A blocked destination, wrong facing or absent extraction step can leave stock stationary. Use a Crude Manipulator where the machine-to-belt transfer needs one. Belts carry items, not fluids or energy; water still needs its own route.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.workshop_flow:
Optional handling: a Crude Manipulator transfers items between the adjacent source and destination in its facing direction. Pair it with correctly oriented belts or inventories to remove repeated hand transfers.

Check source stock, accepting input/output sides and destination space if nothing moves. Avoid feeding a return path that endlessly recirculates needed inputs. Handling automation does not run a recipe, supply water or generate power; keep those requirements visible in the workshop.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.assembly_benc:
The F0 Assembly Bench manufactures primitive construction items from the same authored ingredient definitions as their manual crafts. Load a complete matching batch, supply F0 work and clear output. The live rows below are representative current Bench recipes, not another handwritten recipe graph.

Use it to rebuild tools, pumps and source machines from renewable workshop materials. A blocked output or partial input batch pauses progress. The Assembly Bench does not fabricate a Relay Matrix: the first five-Matrix exit remains a manual crafting-table batch.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.research_term:
The Research Terminal turns a raw ceramic Data Core into a physical Calibrated Data Core using F0 power. Craft it after the workshop can provide boards and glass, then connect working energy supply. The live calibration row gives its full cycle and draw.

The handheld Crank Handle cannot charge this terminal. If starved, inspect actual power; if blocked, take the completed core. Calibration does not unlock a global research permission. Its physical output is consumed by the final manual Relay Matrix craft.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.data_core:
A raw Data Core is made from a ceramic insulator and redstone through the current authored craft; the Bench can manufacture that same component. It is a physical substrate, not a permission or a quest reward shortcut.

Reserve insulators for construction and make another core through renewable workshop inputs if one is lost. Put the raw core into a powered Research Terminal. An uncalibrated core cannot stand in for the calibrated component in the final Matrix batch.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.calibrate:
Feed a raw Data Core to a powered Research Terminal and recover its Calibrated Data Core output. The live row shows the actual work and energy. The Crank Handle is not Terminal power; a completed output must be taken before the next cycle.

This existing quest records possession, not successful operation. Claim its Atlas reward once, then reserve the physical core for manual Matrix assembly. Reading or reclaiming the book never manufactures another calibrated component.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.calibrated_co:
Protect the physical Calibrated Data Core until Matrix assembly. Store it safely or keep it in the intended crafting batch. Its earlier quest claim does not replace the item if it is consumed or lost.

Recovery is production, not a reward reset: make another raw core from workshop insulator and redstone, then calibrate it with actual Terminal power. The same replacement principle applies to lost Matrices: use the real recipe and preserve the one-time claim ledger.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.relay:
T0 ends with the manual five-Relay-Matrix batch using glass, copper, redstone and a Calibrated Data Core. The live crafting row owns the exact ingredient quantities and yield. The Assembly Bench does not fabricate a Matrix; no quest reward replaces this production.

Hold five VALID physical Relay Matrices rated F1 and explicitly claim this existing final T0 quest. Wrong, mixed or malformed ratings do not count. Evidence is not consumed. That individual ledger claim opens the separate T1 tab/chapter; menu access, a different item, another player's progress or T1 prototype claims do not. T1 objectives are not completed T0 content.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1_preview:
This is a preserved T1 objective, not a T0 requirement or a claim that the T1 campaign is finished. The T1 chapter becomes available only after your authoritative final T0 Relay F1 claim. Old IDs and already recorded rewards remain preserved.

Existing inventory objectives and live Atlas routes are retained for compatibility. They do not establish successful operation, accepted T1 progression or an unrestricted new production chain. Finish the T0 source loop and evaluate the current candidate before relying on later-tier prototypes.
